what: Entergy is a regulated utility supplying electricity in Louisiana, Arkansas, Mississippi and Texas, and gas in New Orleans and Baton Rouge. Its territory has attracted large industrial and data centre projects.
customers: Households, businesses and heavy industry along the Gulf Coast, including petrochemical plants and new data centres.
money: regulated electricity generation and delivery in four states
moat: A regulated monopoly in a region where industrial power demand is growing faster than almost anywhere else in the country.
risks: Debt of about $33 billion against $4 billion of cash
Hurricanes regularly damage its network and cost billions to repair
Louisiana and Mississippi regulators set the returns it may earn
Heavy capital spending needs continuous financing
opportunities: Large data centre and industrial projects in Louisiana and Mississippi raise long-term demand
Storm cost recovery mechanisms let it recover much of hurricane damage over time
watch: Industrial and data centre load growth and rate case outcomes.
